fish.name: Hobnail Char
fish.flavor: Named for the pale spots along its flank, laid out like boot-nails on a frozen path. Reliable, unglamorous, and excellent with butter.

fish.name: Meltwater Minnow
fish.flavor: Hatches in spring trickles and spends its whole life tasting of very cold water. Bait shops sell them by the mittenful.

fish.name: Icehole Perch
fish.flavor: Gathers under fresh-drilled holes the way villagers gather under new noticeboards. Nosy, and honestly better for it.

fish.name: Tin Smelt
fish.flavor: Flashes like a dropped spoon all the way down. Fried by the dozen at every thaw festival, eaten faster than that.

fish.name: Woolly Sculpin
fish.flavor: Squat, bristly, and perpetually unimpressed. Locals swear it grows a thicker coat by midwinter, which is not how fish work.

fish.name: Mitten Gudgeon
fish.flavor: Exactly the size and warmth of a lost mitten. Children fish for them with string, bent pins, and pure stubbornness.

fish.name: Powdersnow Chub
fish.flavor: Plump, pale, and soft-spoken. It eats whatever drifts down the ice hole, including one thoroughly documented sandwich.

fish.name: Sleet Shiner
fish.flavor: Travels in slantwise schools that patter against the ice from below. Somehow cold to the touch even after cooking.

fish.name: Bluenose Whitefish
fish.flavor: Its snout turns a deeper blue the colder the season gets. The village consults them as a thermometer of last resort.

fish.name: Kettlepond Loach
fish.flavor: Curls up in the warm lake-bottom mud like tea leaves in a pot. Ice fishermen call catching one 'a good brew.'

fish.name: Skater Bleak
fish.flavor: Glides along the underside of the ice, upside down, shadowing the skaters overhead. It has opinions about your footwork.

fish.name: Frostbite Bitterling
fish.flavor: Small, sour, and proud of both. Traditionally the first catch of the season, and traditionally thrown back with an apology.

fish.name: Graupel Dace
fish.flavor: Speckled like soft hail on a windowsill. Bites at anything, regrets everything.

fish.name: Cairnstone Trout
fish.flavor: Grey and dependable as the stacked stones that mark the mountain pass. Old guides say if you've caught one, you're not lost yet.

fish.name: Auger Trout
fish.flavor: Its spiral flank markings match the ice auger's bite so neatly that some say the drills learned it from the fish. Twists when it fights, so keep your wrist loose.

fish.name: Lanternjaw Burbot
fish.flavor: A droop-faced bottom dweller with a chin like a storm lantern. Ugly in a way the locals affectionately describe as 'ours.'

fish.name: Two-Sweater Pike
fish.flavor: Named for the recommended attire when hauling one up through the ice. It fights like it has an appointment elsewhere.

fish.name: Silverbell Grayling
fish.flavor: Its great sail-fin rings faintly when it leaps at dusk, or so the ferryman insists. He also insists on tips.

fish.name: Needlenose Icefish
fish.flavor: So translucent you can read the weather through it. Fishermen hold them up to the sky to check for tomorrow's clouds.

fish.name: Moraine Barbel
fish.flavor: Roots through glacier-ground gravel for whatever the mountain forgot to keep. Its whiskers know every stone by name.

fish.name: Thaw-Run Salmon
fish.flavor: Arrives with the first meltwater and leaves before the mud dries. Catching one means spring owes you a favor.

fish.name: Yodeler's Loach
fish.flavor: Hums a long, wavering note when lifted from the water. The pitch is terrible. The commitment is admirable.

fish.name: Blue-Lipped Char
fish.flavor: Perpetually looks like it has been out in the cold too long, because it has. Its shiver is technically a swimming style.

fish.name: Glassjaw Pike
fish.flavor: Its jaw is clear as ice-glass, every tooth visible like pins in a frozen windowpane. Handle with respect and the thickest glove you own.

fish.name: Hoarfrost Eel
fish.flavor: Fern-patterns of frost bloom along its back and melt the instant it is landed. Painters weep. The eel shrugs.

fish.name: Bellringer Char
fish.flavor: Once a year the old chapel bell rings from somewhere under the lake, and this fish rises to answer. Nobody has explained the bell, either.

fish.name: Avalanche Darter
fish.flavor: Rides the shockwave through the water when snow thunders down the ridge. Fast, foolhardy, and faintly proud of the noise.

fish.name: Moonhole Whitefish
fish.flavor: Surfaces only in old, abandoned ice holes on moonlit nights. It liked those holes. It misses the company.

fish.name: Grandfather Grayling
fish.flavor: The elders remember their elders complaining about him. Same fish, everyone insists, same disapproving look.

fish.name: Knock-Thrice Charlie
fish.flavor: Locals knock three times on the ice before fishing here: once for luck, once for weather, once for Charlie. Skip the third knock and your bait comes back neatly folded.

fish.name: The Blue Sermon
fish.flavor: An enormous stillness with fins, said to rise once a winter and stare at you until you feel forgiven. Attendance is not optional; the lake decides.

fish.name: Frostsmith's Folly
fish.flavor: Plated in overlapping ice-scales too perfect to be natural. The story goes that a smith once tried to forge the perfect fish, and the lake kept it out of spite.

fish.name: The Long Winter
fish.flavor: When it passes beneath the ice, the whole lake groans and every fishing hole freezes shut behind it. Some winters simply refuse to end, and the locals say this is why.

fish.name: Grandmother Ninefathom
fish.flavor: She has slept in the deepest pocket of the lake since before the village had a name, and the village has been quietly borrowing luck from her ever since. Wake her gently, and remember to say thank you.

fish.name: The Year Without Thaw
fish.flavor: Once a century the lake declines to melt, and this is what it is protecting. Beneath a mile of blue ice, an entire lost springtime swims in the shape of a fish.
